sentences.en: Ancient philosophy is not just about talking or lecturing, or even reading long, dense books.
sentences.zh: 古代哲学不仅仅关乎谈话、讲授，甚至也不仅仅是阅读那些冗长而艰深的书籍。

sentences.en: In fact, it is something people have used throughout history- to solve their problems and to achieve their greatest triumphs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它是一种人们在历史上一直用来解决自身问题并实现最大成就的方法。

sentences.en: Specifically,I am referring to Stoicism, which, in my opinion, is the most practical of all philosophies and therefore the most appealing.
sentences.zh: 具体而言，我所指的是斯多葛主义，依我之见，它是所有哲学流派中最实用、因而也最具吸引力的一种。

sentences.en: Stoicism was founded in Ancient Greece by Zeno of Citium in the early 3rd century BC, but was practised by the likes of Epictetus, Cato, Audioscripts Seneca and Marcus Aurelius.
sentences.zh: 斯多葛主义由古希腊的基提翁的芝诺于公元前3世纪早期创立，但后来由爱比克泰德、加图、塞涅卡和马可·奥勒留等人践行。

sentences.en: Amazingly, we still have access to these ideas, despite the fact that the most famous Stoics never wrote anything down for publication.
sentences.zh: 令人惊叹的是，尽管最著名的斯多葛学派思想家从未为出版而著书立说，我们今天仍能接触到这些思想。

sentences.en: Cato definitely didn't.
sentences.zh: 加图肯定没有著书。

sentences.en: Marcus Aurelius never intended his Meditations to be anything but personal.
sentences.zh: 马可·奥勒留撰写《沉思录》时，本意纯粹是私人用途，绝非为公之用。

sentences.en: Seneca's letters were, well, letters and Epictetus' thoughts come to us by way of a note-taking student.
sentences.zh: 塞涅卡的书信原本只是私人信件，而爱比克泰德的思想则经由一位勤于笔记的学生流传至今。

sentences.en: Stoic principles were based on the idea that its followers could have an unshakable happiness in this life and the key to achieving this was virtue.
sentences.zh: 斯多葛主义的原则基于这样一种理念：其追随者可在现世获得坚不可摧的幸福，而实现这一幸福的关键在于德性。

sentences.en: The road to virtue, in turn, lay in understanding that destructive emotions, like anger and jealousy, are under our conscious control- they don't have to control us, because we can learn to control them.
sentences.zh: 通往德性的道路，则在于理解这样一个事实：愤怒、嫉妒等破坏性情绪处于我们意识的掌控之下——它们不必主宰我们，因为我们能够学会掌控它们。

sentences.en: In the words
sentences.zh: 用爱比克泰德的话来说：

sentences.en: of Epictetus: “external events I cannot control, but the choices I make with regard to them, I do control”.
sentences.zh: ‘外部事件我无法控制，但我对这些事件所作的选择，却完全由我掌控。’

sentences.en: The modern day philosopher and writer Nassim Nicholas Taleb defines a Stoic as someone who has a different perspective on experiences which most of us would see as wholly
sentences.zh: 当代哲学家兼作家纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布将斯多葛主义者定义为这样一类人：他们对大多数常人视作全然负面的经历，持有截然不同的视角。

sentences.en: negative: a Stoic “transforms fear into caution, pain into transformation, mistakes into initiation and desire into undertaking”.
sentences.zh: 斯多葛主义者‘将恐惧转化为谨慎，将痛苦转化为转变，将错误转化为启蒙，将欲望转化为行动’。

sentences.en: Using this definition as a model, we can see that throughout the centuries Stoicism has been practised in more recent history by kings, presidents, artists, writers and entrepreneurs.
sentences.zh: 以这一定义为范本，我们可以看到，在近几个世纪中，斯多葛主义曾被君主、总统、艺术家、作家及企业家广泛践行。

sentences.en: The founding fathers of the United States were inspired by the philosophy.
sentences.zh: 美国开国元勋们深受这一哲学思想的启发。

sentences.en: George Washington was introduced to Stoicism by his neighbours at age seventeen, and later, put on a play based on the life of Cato to inspire his men.
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿十七岁时便由邻居引介接触斯多葛主义，后来更曾排演一出以加图生平为题材的戏剧，以此激励麾下将士。

sentences.en: Thomas Jefferson kept a copy of Seneca beside his bed.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·杰斐逊常年将塞涅卡的著作置于床头。

sentences.en: Writers and artists have also been inspired by the stoics.
sentences.zh: 作家与艺术家同样受到斯多葛学派的启发。

sentences.en: Eugene Delacroix, the renowned French Romantic artist (known best for his painting Liberty Leading the People) was an ardent Stoic, referring to it as his “consoling religion”.
sentences.zh: 著名法国浪漫主义艺术家欧仁·德拉克洛瓦（以画作《自由引导人民》闻名于世）是一位坚定的斯多葛主义者，称其为自己的‘慰藉宗教’。

sentences.en: The economist Adam Smith's theories on capitalism were significantly influenced by the Stoicism that he studied as a schoolboy, under a teacher who had translated Marcus Aurelius' works.
sentences.zh: 经济学家亚当·斯密关于资本主义的理论，深受其少年时代所研习的斯多葛主义影响；当时他的老师曾翻译过马可·奥勒留的著作。

sentences.en: Today's political leaders are no different, with many finding their inspiration from the ancient texts.
sentences.zh: 当今的政治领袖亦不例外，许多人皆从这些古老典籍中汲取灵感。

sentences.en: Former US president Bill Clinton rereads Marcus Aurelius every single year, and many have compared former President Obama's calm leadership style to that of Cato.
sentences.zh: 美国前总统比尔·克林顿每年都会重读马可·奥勒留的著作；许多评论者还将前总统奥巴马沉着冷静的领导风格，与加图相提并论。

sentences.en: Wen Jiabao, the former prime minister of China, claims that Meditations is one of two books he travels with and that he has read it more than one hundred times over the course of his life.
sentences.zh: 中国前总理温家宝声称，《沉思录》是他随身携带的两本书之一，一生中已通读逾百遍。

sentences.en: Stoicism had a profound influence on Albert Ellis, who invented Cognitive Behaviour Therapy, which is used to help people manage their problems by changing the way that they think and behave.
sentences.zh: 斯多葛主义对阿尔伯特·埃利斯产生了深远影响；他正是认知行为疗法的创始人，该疗法通过改变人们的思维与行为方式来帮助其应对问题。

sentences.en: It's most commonly used to treat depression.
sentences.zh: 它最常用于治疗抑郁症。

sentences.en: The idea is that we can take control of our lives by challenging the irrational beliefs that create our faulty thinking, symptoms and behaviours by using logic instead.
sentences.zh: 其核心理念在于：我们可通过逻辑，挑战那些导致错误思维、症状及行为的非理性信念，从而掌控自己的人生。

sentences.en: Stoicism has also become popular in the world of business.
sentences.zh: 斯多葛主义在商界亦日益流行。

sentences.en: Stoic principles can build the resilience and state of mind required to overcome setbacks because Stoics teach turning obstacles into opportunity.
sentences.zh: 斯多葛主义原则有助于培养克服挫折所需的韧性与心态，因为斯多葛学派主张将障碍转化为机遇。

sentences.en: A lesson every business entrepreneur needs to learn.
sentences.zh: 这是每位商业创业者都必须掌握的一课。

sentences.en: I would argue that studying Stoicism is as relevant today as it was 2,000 years ago, thanks to its brilliant insights into how to lead a good life.
sentences.zh: 我认为，研习斯多葛主义在当今时代的重要性，丝毫不亚于两千年前，这得益于它对如何过好一生所提出的卓越洞见。

sentences.zh: 这种思维方式最根本的根基在于一个极为……
